questions.explanation: 'Each of the' emphasizes individual members of a group.
questions.q: ___ of the students received a certificate.

questions.explanation: 'Every' treats all members as a group with a rule applying to all.
questions.q: ___ student must submit the form by Friday.

questions.explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb: 'Neither... is correct'.
options: Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither of the answer is correct.
Neither of the answers is correct.

questions.explanation: 'Either' means one of two options.
questions.q: You can take ___ route; both lead downtown.

questions.explanation: 'Neither of them' means not one nor the other knew.
The fixed reciprocal phrase is 'each other'.
'Each side' emphasizes the two sides individually.
questions.q: ___ side of the river was flooded.

questions.explanation: 'Every' stresses that the rule applied to all children without exception.
'Each of' (not 'every of') is used before 'the' or 'of'.
'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'Each... has'.
options: Each of the players have a number.
Each of the player has a number.
Each of the players has a number.
Each of the players having a number.

questions.explanation: 'Each' individualizes: 'Each book... is mine'.
questions.q: ___ book on the shelf is mine.

questions.explanation: 'Neither of the answers' means not one nor the other was correct.
'Every day' expresses regular frequency.
'Neither of the two' means none of them appeals.
questions.q: I've tried both options and ___ of them appeals to me.

questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular noun: 'Every student'.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Each' stresses the applicants were handled individually.
'Neither of my parents' = not one nor the other.
'Each' refers to every individual person: 'Each knows the risks'.
'Every one of' takes a singular verb: 'was invited'.
options: Every one of them were invited.
Every ones of them was invited.
Every one of them are invited.
Every one of them was invited.

questions.explanation: 'Each window' individualizes every single window.
questions.q: ___ window in the house was broken.
